docs(evidence): settle the Q1x second adversarial axis on measurement

The Q1x artifact decided output 5 per family on two axes: membership-proof
depth, remediated by published-chunk carriage, and spend-input preimage
cardinality, which was recorded as "still unexercised" with an expectation
attached about where it would bind. Both halves move here.

The carriage block gains Q10 and Q11, so `unmeasuredFamilies` is empty for the
first time: the depth axis is now settled for all four families by a
remediation the gate re-derives and that is measured end to end for each of
them. The block records what makes those two journeys different — their trie
openings share one root, and Q11's second opening is an ABSENCE — because a
reader who assumed the zero-input shape would not be able to reproduce them.

`spendInputCardinalityBound` is the new block, and it settles the second axis
the only honest way available: by measuring it and finding that it does not
fit. The gate re-derives every number in it. The admissible cardinality must be
the SMALLEST of the constraints the block lists, so naming a larger one cannot
understate what a proof has to survive. The 862 the field-bytes bound admits is
recomputed from the bytes. The reserve ceiling is recomputed from the ledger's
cap and the same 20% this artifact applies everywhere, and the cap must be
below the consensus profile's capability floor so the boundary is conservative.
Each family's boundary must be an adjacent PAIR whose lower member measures
inside the reserve and whose upper member measures outside it AND inside the
ledger's hard cap — a number above the cap would prove nothing about the
reserve. The verdict is then recomputed from those measurements rather than
read, and the finding must carry the cardinalities it was built on.

`axisIsSettledFor` no longer consults the depth bound for every axis. Each axis
names the bound block that decides it, an unknown bound is a hard failure, and
an axis whose own bound records that the worst admissible instance does not fit
is unsettled however thoroughly it was measured. Under that rule Q12 and Q14
stay LOCAL_PASS and Q10 and Q11 stay OPEN — the same two cells as before, now
for a measured reason rather than an unexamined one.

Seeded mutations of the new block are rejected with their own diagnostics:
flipping the verdict without moving the numbers, claiming carriage remediates
the axis, raising the measured ceiling to the admissible shape, dropping the
20% reserve from the ceiling, downgrading the finding's severity, and removing
a family from the carriage-measured set. The gate's existing vitest self-tests
and its positive control are unchanged and still pass.

The Q10 and Q11 manifest rows replace their stale "the emulator journey still
drives the redeemer-carried route" anchor with the measured stage lists, add
the cardinality derivation and its verdict, and cite both suites.

Refs #549

fix(evidence): recapture the F20 category and directory inventories

The #510 ABI-freeze gate measured two drift findings against the F20
reconciliation: `bindingInventory.registeredCategoryNames` recorded 8
categories where the frozen catalogue order carries 11 after #547, and
`deployedValidatorDirectories` recorded 14 where the index carries 16
after #545 added `mpf-chunked-proof` and the `reference-input-no-idx`
harvest landed. Both inventories are re-derived here by the gate's own
producing derivations — the SDK catalogue's
`FRAUD_PROOF_CATALOGUE_CATEGORY_ORDER` literals and a directory read of
`onchain/aiken/validators/fraud-proofs` — never hand-edited, so the
recapture measures the tree rather than restating it.

Re-running those derivations exposed two adjacent inventories the same
two changes had moved. `unregisteredValidatorDirectories` drops
`invalid-signature` and `no-reference-input`, which #547 registered, and
gains `mpf-chunked-proof`, which is shared chunked carriage rather than a
family: six residues become five. `nativeV1Families` gains
`reference-input-no-idx` as the twelfth transaction-proof chain, so the
standalone-family count is 13.

The native-V1 derivation is repaired rather than merely re-run. #545
introduced `pass_native_tx_to_next_step_carried`, the carriage seam that
takes the membership opening by whichever route the prover chose and
funnels the redeemer-carried one straight back into
`pass_native_tx_to_next_step`. The old call regex could not see the
suffixed identifier, so re-running it as it stood would have published a
9-family inventory that silently dropped `double-spend`,
`invalid-range`, `no-input` and `zero-input` — four families that are
still native V1. The regex now accepts either spelling, the carriage seam
gets its own exactly-one-definition pin beside the helper's, and the
"exactly one transition per step-01" measurement survives the reroute.

With the inventories recaptured the ABI freeze measures no drift at all,
so `driftFindings` is the empty array that claims nothing drifted and the
completed F20 recapture leaves `nextActions`. No waiver is involved:
`waivers` stays empty and `freezeStatus` stays BLOCKED, because IG2 still
measures 11 integrated families without valid-block rejection, maximum
proof-fit or correction evidence. The freeze self-test's drift mutation
is inverted to match — with 0 findings measured there is nothing to
delete, so the seeded defect is now an artifact that invents a finding
the tree does not support, which the same equality rejects.

CG4 binds the freeze by digest and drift count, so its binding is
re-measured, and the CG4 row's count contract carries the 0 the gate now
reports.

Measured: reconciliation 70 rows / 49 open, exit 0; ABI freeze exit 0
with 11 catalogue categories, 16 validator directories, 0 relation
violations, 0 drift findings, 0 waivers; freeze self-test 2 controls / 23
mutations; CG4 gate exit 0 and its self-test 2 controls / 18 mutations;
manifest quality 186 tasks / 0 defects.

test(fault-proofs): measure the spend-input cardinality axis for Q10 and Q11

The Q1x artifact has carried a second adversarial axis since issue #482 with
nothing but an expectation attached to it: spend-input preimage cardinality,
affecting Q10 and Q11, "expected to bind on the spend-inputs WITNESS
publication transaction and on execution units rather than on the step
transaction itself". That expectation is now measured through the real
prepare/submit pipeline, and half of it is wrong.

The admissible cardinality is derived from three protocol constraints and the
smallest is taken: `maxSpendInputCount` 16,384, which its own source calls a
one-byte-per-item encoding floor; `maxSpendInputsPreimageBytes` 32,768, which
at 38 bytes per canonical `TransactionInput` admits 862; and the 296-input
Cardano script-spend shape already pinned as
`maximum_cardano_spend_redeemer_count` and already treated by family Q13 as the
shape a proof must handle.

Measured against the 20% execution reserve over Cardano's own 14,000,000-unit
memory cap — below the consensus profile's 16,500,000 floor, so conservatively:

| family | largest fitting | first over reserve | binding stage |
| ------ | --------------- | ------------------ | ------------- |
| Q10    | 39              | 40                 | step-04       |
| Q11    | 40              | 41                 | step-02       |

At 39 inputs Q10's step-04 measures 11,049,259 memory against an 11,200,000
ceiling; at 40 it measures 11,312,784, over the reserve and still under the
ledger's hard cap. Q11's step-02 measures 11,170,542 at 40 and 11,465,641 at 41.
At the admissible 296 neither family's proof can be evaluated at all: both
exceed the ledger's own memory cap, which the suite asserts by driving them.

What was expected to bind does not. The witness publication transaction is
1,862 bytes at Q10's boundary with 14,522 bytes of margin, and the steps that
reference it are within five bytes of their minimal-fixture size, because the
preimage is a reference input's datum. Q11 is not shaped that way at all: its
step-02 carries `inputs_preimage` in the STEP REDEEMER, so the axis does reach
that transaction's bytes — and still does not bind, with 10,684 bytes of margin
at the boundary. Execution MEMORY binds, in both families, an order of magnitude
below the admissible shape, because a step must re-hash the whole authenticated
bounded collection before it may select one item from it.

That cost is not carriage. Published-chunk carriage remediated Q1X-F5 by moving
bytes out of the step transaction; there is nothing to move here.

The two family fixtures take an optional `spendInputCardinality`, placing the
selected input last so both the collection re-hash and the selection walk are
at their worst.

docs(evidence): rebind the CG4 row to the measured freeze and gate

The CG4 manifest row named two prescribed surfaces that did not exist and
carried a count contract written before either of them was built. It now
leases the four gate scripts and two artifacts that were delivered, and
its evidence outputs and count contract carry the numbers the gates
actually measure rather than the numbers the row expected.

The measured citations: 9 C60–C68 rows reconciled with 0 PASS, 6 rows
carrying an absent prescribed surface, 9 rows dependency-blocked, QG1
unmeasured because its own verifier is absent from the index, 7
cross-package ABI identities re-derived and agreeing, 6 derived relations
with 0 violations, 11 catalogue categories bound onto 16 validator
directories, 393 blueprint validators, 16 IG2 families with 0 integrable
and 11 violations, 2 measured drift findings against the F20 inventory,
and self-tests rejecting 18 and 23 seeded defects against 2 control runs
each.

The row's invalidation triggers gain the ABI surface: because the freeze
re-derives all seven identities from source on every run, any change to
them, to the catalogue-to-validator-tree bijection, to the pinned
compiler or to the blueprint validator set re-opens the IG1 half.
`blockedBecause` is unchanged — CG4 remains blocked on exactly the same
non-PASS queue rows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

ci(evidence): run the ABI freeze and CG4 gates

An uninvoked gate and a gate that cannot fail are the same defect, so
both new gates and both self-tests are wired into the two places the
repository already enforces evidence integrity from.

In Evidence Integrity CI the split follows what each gate needs. The CG4
gate is pure-node and joins the `verify` job, whose unfiltered
pull_request trigger means every change to the task manifest, the
reconciliation or the ABI freeze is gated. The ABI freeze needs a real
`aiken build`, which `verify` has no compiler for, so it joins the
`header-v1-abi` job that already installs the pinned v1.1.22 compiler and
builds the SDK; the gate fails closed when the blueprint is absent rather
than skipping the check.

In the Goal verification plan the ABI freeze runs at the end of the
`capability` phase, which is the phase that produces the blueprint, and
the CG4 gate runs in `evidence` alongside the strict format registry.
Placing the freeze in `evidence` would have left a standalone
`goal:verify:evidence` run without a blueprint to measure.

The freeze's blueprint leg pins the validator set and the compiler rather
than the blueprint bytes. `plutus.json` is a gitignored build output whose
bytes depend on the selected aiken environment — measured at 393
validators and an identical title digest under both `--env testnet` and
the default env, with differing file digests — so pinning the bytes would
fail CI on a legitimate build that chose a different env. The digest is
still recorded, and must be a real one, for attribution.

Refs #510

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(evidence): add the CG4 fund-safety and classification gate

GOAL_SPEC §8.4 CG4 requires no missing or partial fund-safety or
classification row for canonical V1, and the B34 acceptance criteria ask
for C60–C68 and QG1 to close it with one consolidated ABI/fund-safety
review. That review did not exist: the nine classification rows were
tracked only in the task manifest, and nothing measured whether their
prescribed surfaces were actually in the tree.

Following the WG1/IG3 inversion, this gate does not decide that fund
safety is closed. It decides that the published artifact tells the truth
about what has and has not been measured. Each row's acceptance,
dependency set and prescribed surfaces are re-derived from the F05
manifest, so a row cannot restate its own contract; its missing surfaces
are measured against the git index, so a row can neither hide a surface
it lacks nor invent one it already has; and no row may be PASS while a
prescribed surface is absent or a declared dependency is unmet.

QG1 gets the same treatment. Its own local-coverage verifier does not
exist in the tree, so QG1 is UNMEASURED rather than merely open, and the
gate refuses to let it be promoted regardless of what the artifact says.
The consolidated ABI half is bound by digest to the IG1/IG2 freeze, since
CG4's acceptance is a joint review rather than two separate ones.

The gate is local-only by construction: it rejects an artifact that
creates a C70 trusted snapshot, that publishes any live or readiness
claim, or that cites a testnet artifact at all.

Current measurement refuses PASS. All nine rows are dependency-blocked in
the manifest, six are missing at least one prescribed surface, QG1 is
unmeasured against a reconciliation carrying 49 open rows, and the bound
ABI freeze is BLOCKED with 11 IG2 violations. What is closed here is
CG4's own deliverable — the exact one-to-one reconciliation and the
zero-debt report. The C60–C68 implementations belong to the
forced-execution semantics and coverage rows that block them and are
deliberately not attempted.

The self-test drives the real gate against 18 seeded promotions and two
control runs.

Refs #510

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(evidence): bind the canonical V1 ABI freeze across packages

GOAL_SPEC §11 IG1/IG2 asks for one ABI freeze covering every encoder,
decoder, parser, constructor, resolver index and catalogue order, and for
a proof-family gate that refuses to integrate a family missing any of its
six evidence dimensions. The program already pins each surface
individually — F02 owns the 132-row format registry, the HeaderV1 gate
owns the three-way HeaderV1 contract, sdk-abi-fixtures owns the 86 golden
encodings — so this is a binding layer over those pins rather than a
second copy of their numbers.

It closes two holes a per-package pin cannot see. First, the deployment
ABI identity is declared three times: midgard-core, midgard-node and
midgard-sdk each carry their own copy of the 55-entry contract vector,
the 11-entry catalogue order, the 37-role reference-script map, the
38-role auth-token map, the 18 manifest root keys, the 6 step names and
the 12 transaction-order contracts, and nothing anywhere compared the
copies. The #547 registration could have landed in one package and not
another. Second, the frozen catalogue order was never bound to the
validator tree that implements it, so a family directory could be added
or renamed without any gate noticing the catalogue no longer covered it.

Every number the artifact publishes is re-derived from source on each
run: identity vectors are read out of the committed bytes with a scanner
that understands strings and comments, the catalogue-to-tree bijection is
checked both ways against `git ls-files`, and the blueprint identity is
measured from the build the pinned compiler produced. A `record` identity
is compared as a mapping rather than as an ordered list, because every
consumer reads it by key — but the declaration order is measured and
published anyway, which is how ABI-04 now records that core and the SDK
list the same 38 roles in different orders.

Current measurement is deliberately not clean. IG1's structural half
holds: 7 identities agree, 6 derived relations report 0 violations, 11
catalogue categories map one-to-one onto the validator tree's 16
directories, and the 393-validator blueprint came from the v1.1.22
compiler aiken.toml declares. IG2 is BLOCKED: 11 families are registered
in the frozen catalogue while none of them carries valid-block rejection,
maximum proof-fit or correction evidence. Two drift findings against the
F20 inventory are measured by the gate rather than asserted in the file,
so they cannot be closed by editing the artifact.

The self-test drives the real gate against 23 seeded mutations and two
control runs. Two of the mutations seed exactly one package's identity
source and leave the others real, so the cross-package comparison cannot
be satisfied by the artifact alone.

Refs #510

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(fault-proofs): carry Q10 and Q11 openings on published chunks

Issue #545 wired all four foundational families onto published-chunk carriage
on-chain and measured the route end to end for zero-input and invalid-range.
Double-spend and no-input were left on the redeemer-carried route off-chain:
their step builders had the new carriage sum's redeemer arm and nothing else,
so the two families the second adversarial axis affects had no measured chunked
lifecycle at all.

`submit-step-01`, `submit-step-02`, `ne-submit-step-01` and `ne-submit-step-04`
gain the same prover-chosen carriage the other two already had — the chunked
arm references the publication UTxOs, names their order as indices into
`tx.reference_inputs`, and swaps the delegated `phas`/`pexcludes` withdrawal
for the merkelized `mpf_chunked_verify` one. `ne-submit-step-04` is the first
ABSENCE opening to take the route, so `chunkedNonMembershipClaimRedeemer`
carries the pinned absent-value digest rather than a hash of a value.

The carriage helpers move to `proof-chunk-carriage.ts`. They were in
`publish-proof-chunks.ts`, which selects a fee input through
`submit-step-01.ts`; a step builder importing them back would have closed a
module cycle. `publish-proof-chunks.ts` re-exports the module unchanged, so
every existing importer is untouched.

Both families are then driven end to end at forced branch level 22 — past every
family's direct-route envelope ceiling — in
`submit-init-emulator-chunked-proof-carriage.test.ts`. Neither family opens the
challenged block's transactions trie only once, which is what made this more
than a copy of the zero-input journey: double-spend opens it twice for
membership (tx1 at step-01, tx2 at step-02) and no-input opens it once for
membership and once for absence (the phantom input's producing transaction, at
step-04). Two independent synthetic ladders cannot serve, because each ladder
determines its own root and every step re-authenticates against the one root
the challenged header commits. `syntheticDeepSharedRootProofsV1` builds what a
real trie would hold instead: one shared branch node whose child slots carry the
sub-trie digests of the individual ladders, with each opening's top-level
neighbours read out of that same node. The library's own `Proof.verify` is what
confirms every opening reconstructs the one root.

Measured, every stage inside the envelope and the 20% execution reserve:
double-spend publish 3402, init 7862, step-01 13098, publish 3402, step-02
13135, step-03 4244, step-04 9295, remove 1868; no-input publish 3402, init
7862, step-01 13187, step-02 4212, step-03 3929, publish 3402, step-04 13594,
remove 1868. The zero-input and invalid-range journeys re-run byte for byte.
